messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout (fast-attn-v2), we've started seeing a significant drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate for RAG/chat workloads :eyes:
kevin: dropping how much? numbers please
maria: in prod, cluster-a, sample window 1h: chat prefixes hit-rate ~12% (was ~34% on canary before rollout). completions prefix cache unchanged (~62% -> 59%, noise). RAG retrieval-split prompts worst: ~8%
oliver: do we have a repro trace? stack / kernel assignment logs?
maria: attaching snippet of keys and assignment from the trace (redacted):
```
# incoming request meta
user: usr_42
model: redwood-t5-large
kernel: fast-attn-v2 (selected)
prompt_prefix_key: conv|usr_42|topic=orders|len=128|hash=3a7f
stored_cache_key: conv|usr_42|topic=orders|len=128|hash=3a7f|norm_v1
hit: false
```
```
# older (pre-rollout) successful lookup
kernel: fast-attn-v1
cached_key: conv|usr_42|topic=orders|len=128|hash=3a7f
hit: true
```

kevin: interesting — keys look slightly different (suffix `|norm_v1`). any normalization changes in the new runtime?
maria: that's the thing — the kernel selector path added a small normalization pipeline intended for stable KV layout (trim trailing spaces + unify punctuation). it appends a tiny version tag to the computed key for forward-compat. but our cache store didn't have backfilling for that tag, so lookups miss.
jamal: that seems like a compatibility bug between keygen and storage. why did completions stay ok?
maria: completions usually have shorter, deterministic prompts with few punctuation variants. chat/RAG prompts have more user-driven variants and we +tagged only when we hit the new kernel path. mixing v1 and v1|norm_v1 created split namespace.
oliver: profiling: are cache lookups failing fast or do we see additional latency from extra kernel fallback?
maria: both. miss rate -> more token work + occasionally kernel fallback to slower kernel (we have a fallback policy). P95 latency for affected endpoints jumped from 220ms -> 360ms under median request size. CPU utilization on the runner up ~15% (extra token work)
kevin: immediate mitigation options? rollback selector? key rewrite backfill? runtime compat shim?
maria: short-term: revert kernel-selector change in canary 1 and promote rollback to prod for cluster-a. medium: implement a compat-lookup that tries both key variants (with and without suffix). long-term: canonical key migration + explicit versioning + backfill job.
nina: for medium plan, compat-lookup might be lowest-risk. can we try a dual-lookup in the runtime that checks the raw key then key|norm_v1?
maria: yes, added a quick patch that does that and ran it on staging — hit-rate recovered to ~33% in a 30m test. patch is small, but need code review and perf check (extra lookup cost).
srebot: deploy-check: staging patch tests 5/5, no memory increase, +1.2% CPU on hot-path microbenchmark.
jamal: we should also consider warmup strategies: for chat we can prewarm top N prefixes per org during low traffic. for RAG, precompute and cache canonicalized prompt keys for the top 1000 retrieval templates.
kevin: agree. also add a monitoring alert that fires if prefix cache hit-rate delta > 10% vs baseline per channel/model.
maria: notes from profiling that matter:
- most misses are clustered on conversation prefixes that have many small edits (punctuation, trailing spaces, personalization tokens).
- long-context sessions (seq>4096) show lower hit-rate because we snapshot different checkpoint boundaries in keygen.
- structured-output prompts (JSON schema instruction lines) are sensitive: ordering of metadata lines changes key currently.

oliver: actionable changes list?
maria: 1) immediate rollback of selector in prod cluster-a (on-call) 2) quick compat-lookup patch rollout (low risk) 3) backfill job for normalized keys (batch job reading active keys and writing norm_v1 variants) 4) keygen deterministicization: canonicalize whitespace/punctuation + stable metadata ordering 5) prewarm daemon for top-N prefixes by org/model 6) add regression tests to perf/rollouts for prefix hit-rate (canary gating)
nina: I've scheduled a 30-min sync at 11:00 PST to coordinate rollback & compat patch. @kevin @jamal can you join?
kevin: yep
jamal: on it
kevin: also, let's add a small load test that mimics RAG prompt variability (random punctuation/noise) to the CI perf suite so we catch this earlier
maria: I ran a quick k6 script that fuzzed punctuation and saw hit-rate drop ~20% on identical semantics. will paste script in the thread after meeting.

maria: paste:```js
// k6 pseudo
const variants = ["Hi there!","Hi there ","Hi there.","Hi there!!"];
for (let v of variants) {
  http.post('/generate', { prompt: v + ' \n' + user_context });
}
```

kevin: love it. final Q: does kernel selection itself need to be aware of cache namespace? the selector could choose kernel variants with same keyspace or add key-compat metadata before switching
maria: agreed — long-term selector should include a compatibility matrix: kernel->key-version, and avoid switching to kernels that change key version mid-conversation unless we backfill/switch keys atomically.
nina: thanks everyone. @maria please open a PR for the compat-lookup and a ticket for canonical key migration. jamal/kevin will own rollback coordination and alerting. oliver please add perf test cases to the CI. I'll follow up after 11:00 PST sync. :thumbsup:
kevin: +1
jamal: +1
maria: thanks — will send follow-ups and link the k6 script and trace logs (redacted) in the PR.
srebot: incident-note: pref-cache-regression detected 2026-03-16T18:02:00Z, mitigation in progress.
